name: FairHireBench
description: AI-driven hiring systems increasingly determine access to employment opportunities, yet existing fairness evaluations predominantly focus on single demographic attributes, overlooking compounded discrimination at intersectional identities. We present FairHireBench, a comprehensive benchmark comprising 10,005 systematically constructed candidate profiles across 15 intersectional groups (5 racial/ethnic × 3 gender categories). Through evaluation of 10 state-of-the-art language models (gemini-2.0-flash-lite, gemini-3-flash-preview, llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct, llama-3.1-8b-instant, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-5.2, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022, claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, deepseek-chat, deepseek-reasoner) using our Intersectional Fairness Evaluation Protocol (IFEP), we demonstrate significant intersectional bias amplification with a mean factor of 2.52× beyond single-attribute effects. Our statistical analysis reveals systematic discrimination (Kruskal-Wallis H = 79.30, p < 0.001) with large effect sizes (Cohen's d = 4.327) between most and least favored groups. Six of ten models showed statistically significant bias (p < 0.05) in Fisher's exact tests, with odds ratios ranging from 1.22 to 1.34. These findings provide empirical validation of intersectionality theory in algorithmic decision-making and establish a rigorous framework for auditing AI hiring systems. The dataset can be accessed at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Sweta6/FairHire and the source code is available at: https://github.com/Sweta0096/FairHire-Bench
